messages:
incident-bot: Paging: High error rate detected for Hyperion Systems (dedicated-pool: hyperion-prod-1). 5xx spike at 2026-03-15T02:08Z. Pager duty: oncall-alex. Please acknowledge and start mitigation.

oncall-alex: ack. seeing spike in inference errors and increased tail latency. hitting ~12% 5xx across pool. starting triage.

oncall-alex: quick check: are these model-level failures or infra? logs show a lot of gRPC stream resets. attaching sample:
```
2026-03-15T02:06:12Z hyperion-prod-1 node-3 grpc: stream reset: context canceled
2026-03-15T02:06:13Z hyperion-prod-1 node-5 runtime: kvcache OOM warning
```

eng-jordan: I can take runtime side. seeing a pattern: nodes 3/5 have elevated GPU memory pressure, KV cache misses flooding CPU. possibly a bad prompt blast from customer or a small traffic spike that caused extreme cache churn.

sre-maya: checking node-level metrics now. node-3 shows frequent oom_kill events earlier. looks like we hit a quantized-model memory regression after last nights rollout? Deploy bot shows a model push to hyperion-pool at 2026-03-15T01:45Z.

deploy-bot: model-deploy: model:redwood-quant-v2 -> hyperion-prod-1 @ 2026-03-15T01:44:58Z (rollout: 10%)

eng-jordan: that matches. request: pause rollout and route new requests away from nodes with high OOM. oncall-alex, can you put the pool into partial-isolate mode?

oncall-alex: putting pool into isolation (soft) to stop new placements. command:
```
redwoodctl pool set-isolation hyperion-prod-1 --mode soft
```

oncall-alex: also applying immediate routing policy to fallback to hosted model-group for Hyperion tenant traffic to preserve customer requests while we fix pool.

cs-lina: flagging Hyperion CS leadership. Lina -> Im on this. Whats customer-visible impact? Are we failing requests or just latency?

oncall-alex: primary effect: ~12% request failures (5xx). Most others slowed to 600-900ms. We started routing non-critical live traffic to hosted fallback after 02:20Z, so impact is reduced for some flows. Still seeing retries from customer side.

pm-dan: should we do an explicit failover for the entire tenant to hosted while we stabilize? That reduces isolation risk but has cost/latency tradeoffs.

director-ops-raja: yes do the failover if it eliminates errors for the customer ASAP. minimize user-facing errors; we can negotiate credits later. prioritize customer experience.

oncall-alex: initiating tenant-level failover to hosted models for all Hyperion production routes:
```
redwoodctl routing set-tenant-route hyperion --target hosted-fallback-group --priority emergency
```

oncall-alex: confirmed routing change propagated at 2026-03-15T02:25Z. observed immediate drop in 5xx to ~1.2% for routed traffic.

sre-maya: while routing helps, we still need to remediate the pool. eng-jordan, can you roll back the quantized model and drain problematic nodes?

eng-jordan: yes. plan:
- rollback model on hyperion-prod-1 to redwood-quant-v1
- cordon and drain node-3 and node-5
- trigger a cache warmup for remaining nodes

eng-jordan: rollback command:
```
redwoodctl model rollback hyperion-prod-1 --target redwood-quant-v1 --wait
```

eng-jordan: cordoning nodes:
```
redwoodctl node cordon node-3 node-5
redwoodctl node drain node-3 node-5 --force
```

oncall-alex: executing now. expect ~3-4 minutes to drain.

sre-maya: monitor for eviction cascades. if drains cause spike, we may need to spin up temporary spare nodes.

oncall-alex: drains completed at 02:40Z. rollback started.

deploy-bot: model-rollback: hyperion-prod-1 -> redwood-quant-v1 @ 2026-03-15T02:42:10Z

eng-jordan: rollback complete. I'm seeing KV cache back to normal hit ratios. tail latency normalizing.

oncall-alex: running gradual rejoin of nodes after post-drain healthchecks. nodes look stable.

sre-maya: running post-mortem checklist: collecting heap, OOM traces, and canary performance datasets. storing artifacts here: https://internal.redwood/incident/1795550000/artifacts

cs-lina: prepping customer comms. Draft for Hyperion execs: short, what happened, impact, mitigation, next steps, compensation. Will post draft here for review.

cs-lina: DRAFT -> "Hi team — we experienced an elevated error rate impacting some of your requests to the Hyperion production pool between 02:06Z and 02:42Z. Root cause appears to be a model variant rollout that increased GPU memory pressure and caused KV cache churn on two nodes, leading to a spike in 5xxs. We routed customer traffic to hosted fallback to prevent further errors and rolled back the model while draining affected nodes. Services are now stable. Next steps: full RCA, timeline, and compensation proposal. We recommend a post-mortem review with your ops team."

pm-dan: solid. add commitment: "We will issue a 10% service credit for the affected billing window and offer a prioritized review of your pool configuration and suggested ops hardening at no cost."

director-ops-raja: agree to 10% credit. add exec summary line: "No customer data was exposed; this was an operational regression in model rollout."

cs-lina: updated draft posted. Lina -> Hyperion primary contact notified at 03:05Z. customer acknowledged and asked for RCA ETA and any immediate recommendations.

sre-maya: ETA on RCA (initial timeline): 48 hours for preliminary RCA, 7 business days for full postmortem with mitigations and infra changes.

eng-jordan: immediate mitigations well recommend to Hyperion:
- pin model versions for critical routes (prevent automated rollouts)
- enable a smaller rollout window + memory-monitoring abort threshold
- enable tenant-level KV cache reservation (prevent noisy-tenant eviction)

cs-lina: Hyperion asked about an exec-ready summary for their board. Lina requests a 3-paragraph one-liner from Raja for inclusion.

director-ops-raja: posting exec summary: "We had a model rollout that increased memory utilization on two nodes, triggering transient failures in the dedicated pool serving Hyperion. We performed an emergency failover to hosted instances to maintain availability, rolled back the model, drained affected nodes, and stabilized the pool. We will provide an RCA within 48 hours and a remediation plan within 7 days. A 10% service credit for the affected period is offered."

cs-lina: sent to customer at 03:15Z. Hyperion replied: thanks, please include timeline and any suggestions to avoid recurrence.

oncall-alex: action items created and assigned:
- eng-jordan: final logs + patch to rollout gate (24h)
- sre-maya: postmortem artifacts and remediation playbook (48h)
- cs-lina: customer exec email + credit ticket (today)
- pm-dan: coordinate config review with Hyperion ops (48-72h)

pm-dan: also propose we add a feature: "tenant routing circuit breaker" to automatically switch tenants to hosted fallback when per-tenant 5xx rate > threshold. I'll open a feature ticket.

director-ops-raja: good. ensure follow-up with legal/compliance for any SLA wording change.

oncall-alex: incident resolved. monitoring in steady state. closing paging.

cs-lina: follow-up note: Hyperion accepted credit offer and scheduled a configuration review meeting for 2026-03-17T16:00Z.

eng-jordan: leaving a short root-cause pointer for RCA: model-quant-v2 introduced unexpected per-shard memory growth under certain prompt patterns; rollout gating lacked an OOM abort. patch will add memory-based abort and per-tenant cache reservations.

sre-maya: tagging this incident as: customer-impacting, dedicated-pool, rollback, tenant-failover.

director-ops-raja: thanks everyone. please keep notes compact in the incident doc for the RCA. I'll draft the exec-facing one-pager after the 48h preliminary.

oncall-alex: handoff to day-oncall complete. night-oncall was on for initial pages; day-oncall picks up monitoring.

pm-dan: closing checklist: communication sent, credits scheduled, artifact collection in place. We'll reconvene if anything else pops up.

cs-lina: closing thread for now. will reopen if customer requests more detail. :white_check_mark:
